title: converge-multi-sdk-stream-homeostasis-and-credential-fallback-ergonomics
author: Elena Park
release_notes: TS/Go/Python SDKs: introduce ergonomic stream homeostasis and coordinated credential fallback across pull/push streams; minor API additions for typed stream errors; bump package versions (ts 1.14.0, py 2.9.1, go 0.7.3).
description: Motivation: different SDKs had subtle mismatches in streaming lifecycle hooks and credential fallback timing which caused transient 401s during high-frequency reconnects and poor ergonomics for consumers who need synchronous and asynchronous stream primitives concurrently. This PR implements a cross-language pattern we call 'stream homeostasis' which centralizes three pieces: (1) a light-weight stream lifecycle coordinator that exposes explicit warmup/teardown hooks and an idempotent resume token, (2) a coordinated credential fallback policy that delays hard failure until a short grace window and surfaces a typed transient AuthRetry error, and (3) ergonomic convenience shims: a sync wrapper in Python for common pull-stream patterns, a compact async iterator in TypeScript that emits typed events, and a connection pooling hint for the Go connector. Scope: changes are limited to SDK user-facing helpers and thin runtime adapters; no transport or control-plane changes were made. Implementation highlights: added StreamCoordinator in TS with a minimal public surface (warmup(), resume(token), drain(), close(reason)), introduced TypedStreamAuthError and TransientAuthRetry subclasses, wired credential fallback to a 2-tries-with-1000ms-backoff default but expose policy for overrides, added py.sync_stream context manager that wraps existing async stream generator for backwards-compatible sync usage, and bumped package versions and changelogs. Testing: unit tests across all three SDKs for lifecycle transitions and auth-fallback race simulations; integration smoke tests against local emulator that reproduce previous failure mode; added new CI matrix job (sdk:stream-homeostasis) to run stream stress scenarios at 1000 connections for short duration. Rollout plan: merge to main, publish patch releases for TS/Go/Py, coordinate with SDK integrators to opt-in the fallback policy which is off by default for enterprise private installs. Related: references SUP-4421 incident and patches in redwood-infra to increase token refresh jitter.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice consolidation. Can we reduce the default fallback window from 1000ms to 600ms for the hosted default? Some customers already rely on short timeouts.
Elena Park: We experimented with 600ms; 1000ms gives more headroom for busy GC pauses in embedded runtimes. I made the value configurable and added tests that assert behavior for both values.
Sofia Mendes: The typed error shape is great. Please add a short doc blurb in the TS README showing pattern matching on TransientAuthRetry.
Elena Park: Added a README snippet and an example in examples/stream-reconnect.md in this PR; left a link in the description.
Daniel Ko: Go pool hint is harmless but can you add a comment explaining it's advisory only and does not change connection semantics?
Elena Park: Added inline comment and unit test to ensure no semantic changes; updated PR description to clarify no transport changes.
notes_for_release: Publish TS 1.14.0, Py 2.9.1, Go 0.7.3. Highlight new StreamCoordinator and sync_stream utility in SDK release notes. Backward compatible by default: credential fallback disabled in enterprise-private by default; enable via config.
